quote: To study the buddha way is to study the self. To study the self is to forget the self. To forget the self is to be actualized by myriad things. When actualized by myriad things, your body and mind as well as the bodies and minds of others drop away.
source: Dōgen, Shōbōgenzō, Genjōkōan, section 4, Moon in a Dewdrop (trans. Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi, 1985)

evidence.where: The full text of Actualizing the Fundamental Point read in a PDF of Tanahashi’s Enlightenment Unfolds, whose permissions page states that this essay is reprinted from Moon in a Dewdrop, edited by Kazuaki Tanahashi, copyright 1985 San Francisco Zen Center, by permission of North Point Press; the same wording, lower case buddha way included, is printed by the Terebess Genjokoan collection and by the Upaya Zen Center
evidence.edition: Moon in a Dewdrop: Writings of Zen Master Dōgen, North Point Press, 1985, the Aitken and Tanahashi translation, reprinted in Enlightenment Unfolds, Shambhala, 2000
evidence.locator: Genjōkōan, Actualizing the Fundamental Point, the fourth of the essay’s marked sections, counting from As all things are buddha-dharma

reason: All four sentences are exact in the Aitken and Tanahashi translation, including the lower case buddha way and actualized by myriad things, and section 4 is the right place: it is the fourth section opener of the essay. The card stops before No trace of enlightenment remains, which is where the 1985 and 2010 printings diverge, so the sentence that varies is not in play. The proposal’s page 70 could not be confirmed and is left out of the source. Not shipped, not banned, Dōgen is new to the year.
